**What this is.** The first run of the marker union pilot (`docs/PLAN_marker_union_pilot.md`, steps 1–5) on donors that match the QC-set
benchmark design: 5 BC1 samples per donor. It records how the run was set up, the problems found and fixed while running it, and the
results as of 2026-09-24. Earlier workbooks (01–05) cover the design and the development runs on pair A; this notebook does not repeat them.

::: {.callout-note}
## Outcome (holds as of 2026-09-24)
- Two mexicana donors with 5 BC1 samples each were demultiplexed, aligned and taken through discovery, union, count once, gap filling,
  union founder and pairwise PHG on chr10; RTIGER and bbnil (BC2S2 prior) were run on the same lines for comparison.
- **PHG and RTIGER agree on where the introgressions are**, but PHG breaks RTIGER's TEO segments into TEO / HET / B73 pieces and its
  HET segments into HET / B73 pieces, and it calls short HET spikes at the same ranges in many lines that RTIGER calls all B73.
- **All three callers fall short of the single-locus expectation** for a BC2S2 or BC2S3 family: too much HET, too little TEO, and a TEO
  allele fraction of 7–11 % against 12.5 %. PHG is furthest from the expectation, RTIGER closest; bbnil with the BC2S2 prior sits between.
- These are single families (one BC1 plant per donor), so no dilution of informative sites is expected; the shortfall points to PHG
  over-calling B73 (reference bias) — not yet tested.
- Problems found and fixed on the way: a CRISP BED-coordinate bug, and a union founder that PHG could not use. RTIGER in nilHMM takes
  no breeding-design prior (sawers-rellan-labs/nilhmm#27), so RTIGER here has no generation prior.
:::

## 1. Setup

### 1.1 Donors

Both donors were chosen because the QC-set benchmark (design B) has 5 BC1 pools per founder; donors with fewer BC1 samples serve only the
coverage-mixing question (other session). Every sequenced sample is a pool of 6 plants: a BC1 sample is 6 BC1 plants of one donor family,
and each BC2S3 line (0.4x skim, batch 1) is a pool too.

| donor | taxon | BC1 samples (depth) | BC1 total | BC2S3 lines (0.4x) | 1.2x lines |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Zx.0540_P3** | mexicana | S_2A_3 (11.8x), S_2A_11 (5.5x), S_2B_8 (12.5x), S_2F_1 (8.5x), S_2F_12 (4.9x) | 43.2x | 40 NILs (PN5_SID464–480, PN6_SID481–505) | none |
| **Zx.0570_P2** | mexicana | S_2H_1 (11.9x), S_3B_11 (6.9x), S_3C_9 (9.2x), S_3D_8 (8.0x), S_3E_7 (7.7x) | 43.7x | 44 NILs (PN8_SID733–768, PN9_SID769–778) | none |

Zx.0570_P2 was picked over Zx.0580_P2 as the second donor because its number of NILs (44) is closer to Zx.0540_P3's (40). Two libraries
are very small: PN6_SID484 (Zx.0540_P3, 51,739 read pairs) and PN8_SID736 (Zx.0570_P2, 153,093 pairs).

### 1.2 Data preparation

| step | what | script | jobs |
|---|---|---|---|
| BC1 demux + align | DEMUX of the donors' pools, ALIGN of the 5 samples only (minibwa -x sr, MAPQ 20, CRAM) | `nilhmm/q_nilhmm_pool_run.sh` (POOLS/SAMPLES scoped) | 935092 (2A 2B 2F), 945148 (2H 3B–3E) |
| line realign | batch-1 trimmed FASTQs → minibwa, MAPQ 20, CRAM | `PHG/bin/bc2s3_realign.sbatch` | 935093 (40), 945149 (44) |

Measured times: DEMUX of a 94–140 GB pool 53–72 min (pools in parallel); BC1 ALIGN 56 min – 2 h 39 min at 8 CPUs, about 12–13 min per 1x
of depth; line realign ~10 min per line (array). A full donor prep is about 4 h.

### 1.3 Pipeline (chr10)

| # | step | what | script |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Discovery | BC2S3 artificial pool (all the donor's lines, one RG) → CRISP on the 5 BC1 samples + the pool (lowcopy BED, `-p 12 --sm 0 --mmq 20 --filterreads 0 --minc 2`) → records outside the BED dropped (§3.1) → witness veto (≥ 1 ALT read in the pool) → B73 pools (NCBI ERR3288215 + check pool skim10) counted at the kept sites (`mpileup -I`) → step 4 (LLR tiers; B73 pools = zero class) | `PHG/bin/donor_discovery_chr10.sbatch` |
| 2 | Union | tier-A sites of both donors | `PHG/bin/union_sites.py` |
| 3 | Count once | read counts at every union site in the 10 BC1 samples + 2 B73 pools → joint step 4 | `count_union_sample.sbatch`, `count_once_step4.sbatch` |
| 4 | Gap filling | own sites ALT; gap sites REF if the donor's reads say tier ref, ALT if posterior ≥ 0.999 with the other donor as the prior, else missing | `PHG/bin/dhd_bayes.py` |
| 5 | Union founder | gVCF: one reference block per lowcopy range, split at ALT records, no record at missing sites (§3.2) → pseudo-assembly (B73 + ALT) | `PHG/bin/union_founder_gvcf.py` |
| 6 | PHG | pairwise graph (B73 + the donor's founder), the donor's lines only; find-paths diploid, F = 0, stay 0.99999, min-reads 1 | `PHG/bin/union_founder_phg.sbatch` |
| 7 | RTIGER | per-line pileup at the donor's own tier-A sites, sites with no ALT read across lines dropped, rigidity 500; no design prior (§3.3) | `PHG/bin/rtiger_ancestry_inference.sbatch` |
| 8 | bbnil | same per-line counts as RTIGER; design BC2S2; rrate = 4.72 × L_chr10 / n_markers, L_chr10 = 1.359 M (nilHMM TeoNAM v5 map) → 0.000127 (Zx.0570_P2, 50,308 markers), 0.000168 (Zx.0540_P3, 38,287) | `PHG/bin/bbnil_lines.R` |
| 9 | B73 check | PN10_SID893 (batch-1 B73 control, 0.57x, realigned): RTIGER decoded with the lines' fit, bbnil with the lines' rrate, PHG on the same founder — the lines' results unchanged | `PHG/bin/rtiger_bbnil_check.R`, `union_founder_phg.sbatch` |
| 10 | Painting | per line: RTIGER, bbnil BC2S2, PHG; B73 check pinned on top; label = NIL id + skim coverage (`WGSmetrics_summary.tsv`, old batch-1 BAMs) | `PHG/analysis/paint_rtiger_phg.R` |

Results on hazel: `ZEAL/results/bench_zx0540_chr10/`, `bench_zx0570_chr10/` (prep + discovery) and `union_zx0540_zx0570_chr10/`
(union, count once, founders, PHG, RTIGER, paintings). Runs before the CRISP fix are kept in `discovery/<donor>_preBEDfix/` and
`union_zx0540_zx0570_chr10/preBEDfix/`.

## 2. Results

### 2.1 Discovery (after the CRISP fix; jobs 949447, 949448)

| donor | CRISP records in BED | dropped past range ends | kept by veto | step-4 sites | A | B | C | ref |

### 2.2 Union, count once and gap filling (jobs 949610–949612)

The union holds 82,840 alleles at 82,773 positions (67 multi-allelic); 12,496 alleles are tier A in both donors and 70,344 in one.
In the joint step 4, the two B73 pools come out tier A at 48 sites and tier ref at 60,974.

| donor | own ALT | gaps (union sites it lacks) | gap → ALT | gap → REF | gap → missing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Zx.0540_P3 | 40,874 | 41,832 | 17,517 | 12,496 | 11,819 |
| Zx.0570_P2 | 54,328 | 28,378 | 7,768 | 11,531 | 9,079 |

### 2.3 Union founders and PHG (jobs 949613, 949614)

| donor | founder ALT | REF (inside blocks) | missing (holes) | ranges with a founder haplotype |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Zx.0540_P3 | 58,391 | 12,496 | 11,819 | 8,095 / 8,095 |
| Zx.0570_P2 | 62,096 | 11,531 | 9,079 | 8,095 / 8,095 |

PHG no-call: 24.0 % of ranges (Zx.0570_P2), 30.3 % (Zx.0540_P3). The two small libraries are mostly no-call: PN8_SID736 91 % (736 ranges
called), PN6_SID484 97 % (220 ranges called, all B73).

### 2.4 Genotype distributions against the single-locus expectation

Expectation for one BC2 plant (heterozygous for the donor with probability 1/4), then selfing: HET halves each generation, the other half
splits equally between the homozygotes. The TEO allele fraction is 12.5 % in both generations.

**Zx.0570_P2** (44 lines, chr10)

| | B73 | HET | TEO | TEO allele fraction | lines with TEO calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PHG (share of called ranges) | 87.9 % | 10.2 % | 1.9 % | 7.0 % | 44 / 44 |
| RTIGER | 86.8 % | 9.1 % | 4.1 % | 8.7 % | 16 / 44 |
| bbnil BC2S2 | 88.3 % | 8.1 % | 3.6 % | 7.6 % | 44 / 44 |
| BC2S2 expected | 84.4 % | 6.25 % | 9.4 % | 12.5 % | |
| BC2S3 expected | 85.9 % | 3.1 % | 10.9 % | 12.5 % | |

**Zx.0540_P3** (40 lines, chr10; RTIGER and bbnil on 39 lines, without PN6_SID484)

| | B73 | HET | TEO | TEO allele fraction | lines with TEO calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PHG (share of called ranges) | 86.4 % | 11.2 % | 2.4 % | 8.0 % | 39 / 40 |
| RTIGER | 84.9 % | 8.5 % | 6.6 % | 10.8 % | 20 / 39 |
| bbnil BC2S2 | 85.8 % | 8.8 % | 5.4 % | 9.8 % | 39 / 39 |
| BC2S2 expected | 84.4 % | 6.25 % | 9.4 % | 12.5 % | |
| BC2S3 expected | 85.9 % | 3.1 % | 10.9 % | 12.5 % | |

RTIGER and bbnil shares are of chr10 bp (bbnil segments cover 98.8–98.9 % of chr10 × lines); PHG shares are of called ranges. RTIGER has
no generation prior (§3.3); bbnil uses the BC2S2 prior.

### 2.5 B73 check

| B73 check PN10_SID893 (0.57x) | Zx.0570_P2 graph | Zx.0540_P3 graph |
|---|---|---|
| RTIGER | all B73 (1 segment) | all B73 (1 segment) |
| bbnil BC2S2 | 100.0 % B73 (HET / TEO pieces < 0.05 %) | 100.0 % B73 |
| PHG | HET in 45 of 6,881 called ranges (0.7 %); no-call 15 % | HET in 56 of 6,875 (0.8 %); no-call 15 % |

### 2.6 Paintings

![Zx.0570_P2, chr10, 44 lines + B73 check (top): RTIGER / bbnil BC2S2 / PHG; label = NIL id + skim coverage (local copy).](../../agent/paintings/Zx.0570_P2_chr10_RTIGER_bbnil_PHG.png)

![Zx.0540_P3, chr10, 40 lines + B73 check (top; PN6_SID484 = Zx05403352, PHG only): RTIGER / bbnil BC2S2 / PHG; label = NIL id + skim coverage (local copy).](../../agent/paintings/Zx.0540_P3_chr10_RTIGER_bbnil_PHG.png)

What the paintings show:

- The callers agree on which lines carry introgressions and where.
- bbnil follows RTIGER's introgressions but, like PHG, breaks them into short HET / B73 and TEO / HET pieces, and calls some HET or TEO
  in every line.
- Inside RTIGER's TEO segments (e.g. Zx05702132, Zx05702411, Zx05403561) PHG alternates TEO, HET and B73; inside RTIGER's HET segments
  (e.g. Zx05702242, Zx05702131) PHG alternates HET and B73.
- In lines RTIGER calls all B73, PHG shows short HET (occasionally TEO) spikes at the same positions across many lines — specific ranges,
  not lines. The B73 check shows the same spikes (§2.5).
- PHG counts a line as carrying TEO when a single range is called; RTIGER merges short calls at rigidity 500. That is why PHG reports TEO
  calls in almost every line and RTIGER in about half.

## 3. Problems found and fixed

### 3.1 CRISP reads the BED end one base too far

CRISP converts the BED start correctly (1-based `s+1`) but treats the end as inclusive in 0-based coordinates, so it also calls the base
right after every range. Direct test: BED `chr10 105269 105270` (base 105,270 only) → CRISP reported 105,271. Across the 8,095 ranges,
Zx.0570_P2's raw output had 29 records at range end + 1, near the density inside the ranges (36 at the first base), and 2 before the
start. Source: `variantcalls.c` tests `k >= start && k <= end` with the raw BED values and a 0-based `k`.

- **Fix** (`dc95eea`): right after CRISP, keep only records inside the true ranges (`bcftools view -T <bed>`), before veto, step 4,
  union and RTIGER.
- **Not fixed:** `PHG/qcset/variant_discovery.sbatch` (QC-set discovery) has the same CRISP call.
- **Affected:** every step-4 table made before `dc95eea` and everything built on it. Both donors here were rerun.
- Reported upstream: [vibansal/crisp#34](https://github.com/vibansal/crisp/issues/34). Recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` (2026-09-24).

### 3.2 A union founder PHG could not use

The plan specified the union founder as records only at the union sites (ALT at ALT, REF at REF, nothing at missing). PHG's `gvcf2hvcf`
builds a founder haplotype only from the stretches that have gVCF records, so each haplotype became the recorded 1–2 bp pieces joined
together (a 571-bp range gave ~15 bp). Only 5,179 of 8,095 ranges had a founder haplotype, and reads cannot match such sequences by
k-mers: **zero TEO calls in all 44 Zx.0570_P2 lines** (job 949013, kept in `phg/Zx.0570_P2_records_only_949013/`).

Fix (user decision): one reference block per lowcopy range, split at ALT records, no record at missing sites. Every range then has a
full-length founder haplotype (B73 sequence with the donor's ALT alleles), and a missing site is the only base absent from it. A detour
that built the blocks from the donor's covered stretches (`covered_blocks.sh`, not in the plan) was removed before any run.

Consequence: a range without an ALT site has a founder haplotype identical to B73, and PHG reports it as no call.

### 3.3 RTIGER in nilHMM takes no breeding-design prior

The `rtiger` caller in nilHMM (0.3.0, and the source at `96d5c48`) has only `rigidity`, `seed`, starting emission values, `threads` and
`postprocess`. Start probabilities and transitions are estimated from the data by EM; the number of states is fixed at 3. `design` is
accepted by `call_states()` but silently dropped for `rtiger`. So RTIGER here has no generation prior, and a BC2S2-vs-BC2S3 comparison
(plan step 7) cannot be run with it. Filed as [sawers-rellan-labs/nilhmm#27](https://github.com/sawers-rellan-labs/nilhmm/issues/27):
rtiger should take `design`, and until then should not accept it silently. The RTIGER scripts no longer pass `design` (`abc26df`).

### 3.4 Smaller issues

- **PN6_SID484** covers 253 markers; RTIGER requires 2 × rigidity = 1,000 per line and refuses the whole run. It was dropped from RTIGER
  and keeps its PHG lane.
- **Demux QC overwrite:** every pool run overwrites `results/demux_qc/demux_qc.tsv`; the donors' rows were saved to
  `bench_*/demux_qc_*_20260924.tsv` before the next run.
- **Slurm controller outage** 2026-09-23 20:40–20:53 (`scontrol ping` not responding; `sacct` still answered from the accounting database).

## 4. Caveats

- PHG shares are over called ranges (24–30 % no-call excluded); RTIGER shares are over bp. The paintings fill PHG no-call and
  shared-haplotype ranges with the flanking ancestry (as in `paint_callers_introg.R`), which hides where PHG made no call.
- The shortfall against the expectation cannot come from dilution across families: each donor's lines descend from one BC1 plant and
  carry the same donor haplotype, so a site informative for the donor is informative in every line. Within a family the shortfall is
  unexpected, unless PHG over-calls B73 (reference bias). RTIGER is also below the expectation, though closer.
- The founder's missing sites (9,079 and 11,819) are holes in the founder haplotype. Whether PHG's B73 and HET calls inside RTIGER's
  introgressions sit on ranges with more holes has not been tested.
- chr10 only; one run per donor; the 1.2x data does not exist for these donors.

## 5. Comparison with TeoNAM

TeoNAM ([Chen et al. 2019, *Genetics* 213:1065](https://academic.oup.com/genetics/article/213/3/1065/5930618)): five teosinte × W22 families,
1,257 BC1S4 RILs, genotyped by GBS as individual diploid plants.

**Their pipeline (Methods):**

1. **Variant discovery and joint calling.** Variant discovery was done beforehand, on an external maize/teosinte GBS panel: the 955,690 SNPs
   of the ZeaGBSv2.7 Production TagsOnPhysicalMap file. The TASSEL5-GBS Production Pipeline then called **hard genotypes** at those SNPs
   **jointly on all 1,257 samples**.
2. **Informative sites per family.** Filter on those calls, separately for each subpopulation: MAF ≥ 5 %, sites thinned 64 bp apart.
3. **Imputation per family.** FSFHap (TASSEL5) per chromosome: backcross route, Phet = 0.03125 (the BC1S4 expectation), Fillgaps = TRUE;
   ~13,733 SNPs per family. Genetic maps per family with R/qtl `est.map` (Haldane, error 0.001, BC1S4 pedigree); composite map 1,540 cM.
4. **Joint matrix for linkage mapping (JLM).** The families' sites combined into 51,544 unique SNPs; genotypes coded as parental ancestry
   (W22 homozygous 0, heterozygous 1, non-W22 homozygous 2); the remaining gaps filled from the flanking markers when both flanks agree;
   4,578 markers after breakpoint imputation.
5. **Separate GWAS matrix.** Looser filter (MAF > 0.01, missing < 0.75, heterozygosity < 0.1), FSFHap per chromosome and family again;
   118,838 SNPs.

**The same distortion.** TeoNAM also has excess HET, too little homozygous donor and an excess of the recurrent parent, in every family:

| | recurrent (W22 / B73) | HET | TEO |
|---|---|---|---|
| TeoNAM BC1S4 expected | 73.4 % | 3.1 % | 23.4 % |
| TeoNAM observed | 76.6 % | 8.1 % (2.6× expected) | 15.0 % (0.64×) |
| Zx.0540_P3, RTIGER vs BC2S2 expected | 84.9 % vs 84.4 % | 8.5 % vs 6.25 % (1.4×) | 6.6 % vs 9.4 % (0.70×) |
| Zx.0570_P2, RTIGER vs BC2S2 expected | 86.8 % vs 84.4 % | 9.1 % vs 6.25 % (1.5×) | 4.1 % vs 9.4 % (0.44×) |

They attribute the excess heterozygosity to "unconscious selection for more heterozygous plants that had hybrid vigor", and report the excess
of maize alleles as a feature of all subpopulations.

**Side by side.** Informative here means informative for a biparental cross: a site is informative for a family if it is polymorphic
between the parental gametes (the recurrent parent vs the donor haplotype H_d). A site can be variant at the level of the joint population
(all ZEAL NILs) and still be non-informative for a given donor; in the union, such sites are the donor's gap REF calls. This matches TeoNAM's
segregating sites (a site segregating within a family is polymorphic between its parents); both are measured on progeny (RILs in TeoNAM,
pools of BC1 plants here).


| | TeoNAM | ZEAL (this pilot) |
|---|---|---|
| samples | individual diploid RILs | 6-plant pools (BC1 samples and BC2S3 lines) |
| variant discovery | external panel, done beforehand (ZeaGBSv2.7 TOPM, 955,690 SNPs) | per donor, from these reads (CRISP on the BC1 pools + BC2S3 pool) |
| per-sample data at each site | a hard genotype call (0 / 1 / 2 or missing, from TASSEL-GBS) | REF and ALT read counts; no genotype is called (step 4, gap filling and RTIGER work on the counts) |
| informative sites (segregating sites in a biparental cross) | sites segregating within the family's RILs (MAF ≥ 5 % per subpopulation, on the TASSEL-GBS calls) | sites segregating within the donor's BC1 samples: tier A in step 4 (ALT reads at the BC1 dosage, in ≥ 2 BC1 samples, absent from B73) |
| joint site set | union of the families' segregating sites (51,544) | union of the donors' tier-A sites (82,840) |
| alleles at the other families' / donors' sites | called jointly on all samples at the discovered SNPs (TASSEL-GBS); leftover JLM gaps filled by flank interpolation in ancestry coding | union + gap filling: each donor's allele at the other donors' sites from its own reads (count once), the other donor as the prior for ALT |
| JLM matrix | the per-family ancestry mosaics projected onto the union of segregating sites (flank interpolation where both flanks agree; 4,578 markers) | each donor's RTIGER mosaic projected onto a 0.1 cM grid: the union markers placed on the TeoNAM v5 map and thinned to markers at least 0.1 cM apart (exact 1-D maximum independent set, Jena et al. 2018). Not built yet. |
| GWAS matrix | FSFHap-imputed genotypes per family (BC1 backcross route; 118,838 SNPs) | the PHG-imputed genotypes at the union sites (not built yet) |

**FSFHap on these lines.** nilHMM's `fsfhap` caller was run per donor (lines = one family, design BC2S2) and returned no states. That is
the documented behaviour, not a bug (`nilhmm/design/FSFHAP_PORT.md`): TASSEL takes the backcross route only for a recurrent contribution of
0.75 (BC1), so BC2 falls through to `BiparentalHaplotypeFinder`, which needs two balanced full-sib clusters per window and is documented as
"inappropriate for NILs" (> 90 % of the genome homozygous recurrent in every line; no seed window). TeoNAM works because it is BC1.

## 6. Open questions

1. Reference bias or missing sites: per range, count founder holes and compare ranges where PHG disagrees with RTIGER inside introgressions
   against ranges where they agree; same for the recurring HET spikes in the all-B73 lines.
2. Design prior for the pooled lines (BC2S2 vs BC2S3): waits for RTIGER to take `design` in nilHMM (nilhmm#27). bbnil takes it now
   (BC2S2 run here).
3. The same CRISP fix in `PHG/qcset/variant_discovery.sbatch`, and rerunning the other donors' discovery (other sessions' lanes).
